{
  "findings": [
    {
      "file": "app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb",
      "line": 38,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "api",
      "title": "Legacy membership PATCH requests now silently change visibility",
      "body": "The resources route still sends PATCH requests to update, but the incremental membership handler has been removed. For a visible group, PATCH /admin/groups/:id with changes: {delete: \"alice\"} now ignores the requested removal, sets visible to false because that parameter is absent, and returns success. Existing callers can believe membership was revoked when it remains intact. Preserve the supported PATCH behavior or explicitly reject legacy payloads instead of silently applying an unrelated update."
    },
    {
      "file": "app/controllers/groups_controller.rb",
      "line": 22,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Public member lists are truncated without pagination",
      "body": "This action now limits every group to 50 members, but the public group-members route calls findMembers only once and its template has no pagination or further loading. Nonautomatic groups with more than 50 members therefore lose the remainder of their public member list, whereas previously all members were returned. Add public pagination or incremental loading alongside the endpoint change."
    },
    {
      "file": "app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6",
      "line": 13,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Exact page-size multiples produce an extra empty page",
      "body": "Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1 overcounts pages whenever the member count is an exact multiple of the limit. With 50 members and a limit of 50, the controller reports two pages and enables Next on the only populated page; clicking it requests offset 50 and displays an empty list. Use Math.ceil(user_count / limit), retaining the zero-member handling."
    },
    {
      "file": "app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6",
      "line": 56,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "concurrency",
      "title": "Capture the group before opening the removal confirmation",
      "body": "The confirmation message names the current group, but its callback retrieves the controller's model again. If the administrator navigates to another group while the Bootbox dialog remains open, such as through browser Back, confirming removes the user from the newly selected group rather than the group named in the dialog. Capture the original group before opening the confirmation and invoke removeMember on that captured model."
    },
    {
      "file": "app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js",
      "line": 47,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Membership reloads use an unsaved editable group name",
      "body": "Both membership mutations reload through findMembers, which addresses the group by model.name. The admin name field changes that property immediately, before Save persists the rename. If an administrator edits the name and then adds or removes a member, the mutation succeeds using the group ID, but the reload requests the nonexistent new name and fails, leaving the displayed membership stale. Reload using a persisted identifier or persisted name."
    },
    {
      "file": "app/assets/javascripts/admin/routes/admin_group_route.js",
      "line": 12,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "Reset pending usernames when switching groups",
      "body": "The admin-group controller is reused across group routes, and usernames is now standalone controller state. setupController changes only the model, while addMembers also leaves usernames populated after success. Users selected or added in group A consequently remain selected after navigating to group B and are included in its next Add request, potentially granting unintended membership. Clear the selection when changing groups and after a successful addition."
    },
    {
      "file": "app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js",
      "line": 31,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "concurrency",
      "title": "Ignore stale member-page responses",
      "body": "Next and Previous update the offset immediately and allow another request before the first finishes, while every findMembers response unconditionally overwrites members and offset. Clicking Next twice can request offsets 50 and 100; if the offset-100 response arrives first, the later offset-50 response moves the display back to the earlier page. Serialize pagination requests or track request order so an older response cannot overwrite the latest navigation."
    }
  ]
}

findings.title: Legacy membership PATCH requests now silently change visibility
findings.body: The resources route still sends PATCH requests to update, but the incremental membership handler has been removed. For a visible group, PATCH /admin/groups/:id with changes: {delete: "alice"} now ignores the requested removal, sets visible to false because that parameter is absent, and returns success. Existing callers can believe membership was revoked when it remains intact. Preserve the supported PATCH behavior or explicitly reject legacy payloads instead of silently applying an unrelated update.

findings.title: Public member lists are truncated without pagination
findings.body: This action now limits every group to 50 members, but the public group-members route calls findMembers only once and its template has no pagination or further loading. Nonautomatic groups with more than 50 members therefore lose the remainder of their public member list, whereas previously all members were returned. Add public pagination or incremental loading alongside the endpoint change.

findings.title: Exact page-size multiples produce an extra empty page
findings.body: Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1 overcounts pages whenever the member count is an exact multiple of the limit. With 50 members and a limit of 50, the controller reports two pages and enables Next on the only populated page; clicking it requests offset 50 and displays an empty list. Use Math.ceil(user_count / limit), retaining the zero-member handling.

findings.title: Capture the group before opening the removal confirmation
findings.body: The confirmation message names the current group, but its callback retrieves the controller's model again. If the administrator navigates to another group while the Bootbox dialog remains open, such as through browser Back, confirming removes the user from the newly selected group rather than the group named in the dialog. Capture the original group before opening the confirmation and invoke removeMember on that captured model.

findings.title: Membership reloads use an unsaved editable group name
findings.body: Both membership mutations reload through findMembers, which addresses the group by model.name. The admin name field changes that property immediately, before Save persists the rename. If an administrator edits the name and then adds or removes a member, the mutation succeeds using the group ID, but the reload requests the nonexistent new name and fails, leaving the displayed membership stale. Reload using a persisted identifier or persisted name.

findings.title: Reset pending usernames when switching groups
findings.body: The admin-group controller is reused across group routes, and usernames is now standalone controller state. setupController changes only the model, while addMembers also leaves usernames populated after success. Users selected or added in group A consequently remain selected after navigating to group B and are included in its next Add request, potentially granting unintended membership. Clear the selection when changing groups and after a successful addition.

findings.title: Ignore stale member-page responses
findings.body: Next and Previous update the offset immediately and allow another request before the first finishes, while every findMembers response unconditionally overwrites members and offset. Clicking Next twice can request offsets 50 and 100; if the offset-100 response arrives first, the later offset-50 response moves the display back to the earlier page. Serialize pagination requests or track request order so an older response cannot overwrite the latest navigation.
